title: Overcoming targeted therapy resistance
summary: Understanding why tumours escape targeted therapy, and designing next-generation inhibitors that anticipate those escape routes.
focus: Most patients who respond to first-generation kinase inhibitors eventually relapse. Our oncology programme maps the resistance mechanisms driving that relapse and designs compounds that remain active against them.

milestones.description: Resistance atlas established across 1,400 paired tumour biopsies
NV-204 entered Phase II in previously treated melanoma
ASCENT-3 confirmatory Phase III opened to enrolment

title: Selective immune modulation
summary: Suppressing the pathways that drive chronic inflammation without broadly compromising immune defence.
focus: Broad immunosuppression carries a well-documented infection burden. Our immunology work isolates the specific cytokine axes responsible for tissue damage, aiming for durable disease control with a narrower safety trade-off.

milestones.description: Pivotal trial met its primary endpoint in plaque psoriasis
NV-118 approved for adults with moderate to severe disease

title: Neuroinflammation and glial biology
summary: Investigating the role of microglia in clearing neurotoxic aggregates, and whether restoring that function slows cognitive decline.
focus: Amyloid-directed approaches have produced modest clinical benefit. We are investigating the cells responsible for clearing those aggregates, on the hypothesis that restoring glial function addresses the disease closer to its origin.

milestones.description: TREM2 modulation validated in three preclinical models
